newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CLP sees new investments in China, Asia.
newsitem.headline: CLP sees new investments in China, Asia.

text.p: China Light & Power Co Ltd (CLP) said on Tuesday the proceeds of its share placement with CITIC Pacific Ltd would be used for new investments in China and elsewhere in Asia.

"CLP's financial strength and capable professional management together with CITIC Pacific's relationships in the PRC (People's Republic of China) will put CLP in a very strong position to take full advantage of the substantial opportunities in the power industry in the PRC," CLP chairman Michael Kadoorie said in a statement.
"CITIC Pacific has confirmed it will cooperate with CLP to procure power projects in the PRC."
He said CLP would use the proceeds for new investments in China and elsewhere in Asia.

In a announcement widely anticipated in the Hong Kong stock market, CITIC Pacific said it would acquire 497,664,000 new shares in China Light & Power Co Ltd (CLP) at HK$32.66 each, representing a 20 percent stake in CLP's enlarged share capital, an outlay estimated at HK$16.25 billion.
Kadoorie said his family's interest in CLP would be diluted as a result but the family would remain long-term shareholders and had no intention of selling any shares.
He gave no figures. Prior to the placement, analysts said they estimated the Kadoorie family, one of Hong Kong's long established dynasties, held in the region of 24 percent of CLP.

CLP said CITIC Pacific's chairman Larry Yung, managing director Henry Fan and deputy managing director Vernon Moore would be appointed to the CLP board, but the existing CLP management would remain unchanged.
